subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what key or slash trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The code path is clear, but launching `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR` and writing prompt drafts to disk is a product and security boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX Choice
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the permanent trigger model and safety requirements.

options.title: Decline External Process Handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another product surface over launching local editors from TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest TUI editor ownership trail and already reviewed this exact request.
